about: Answers to the questions people search about sharks (src/tracker19.py tracks them monthly). Shown on /questions/, Home and Safety by answers19.py. Labels follow the claim grades (grade_from); an answer whose claim was regraded, or whose bite counts are older than the database, is held back for review. Each 'fresh.next' date is when to check an outside source for a newer release.

answers.q: How many shark attacks in Australia in 2026?
also: How many shark attacks in Australia per year?
How many shark attacks in Australia this year?
How many shark attacks in Sydney 2026?
answers.a: 8 unprovoked bites from January to June 2026, 7 of them in NSW and 1 in South Australia; one was fatal. The record runs to June, so bites since then aren't counted yet.
detail: 2025: 22 unprovoked bites (10 NSW, 6 WA, 3 SA, 2 Queensland, 1 Victoria), 5 of them fatal.
2016–2025: about 20 a year on average.
The database is updated a few times a year; later 2026 bites will be added when it is.

answers.q: How many shark attacks are there a year worldwide?
also: How many shark attacks per year?
How many shark attacks per year worldwide?
How many shark attacks in 2026?
answers.a: About 60 confirmed unprovoked bites a year. In 2025 there were 65, and 9 were fatal.
detail: 2025: United States 25, Australia 21, the Bahamas 5, New Zealand 3, and one each in 11 other places, including South Africa, Canada and New Caledonia.
The 2020–2024 average was 61 bites and 8 deaths a year.
Counts differ a little by source: this one has 21 for Australia in 2025, the Australian database 22, because they classify some cases differently.
Each year's worldwide count comes out early the next year, so 2026 isn't counted yet.
answers.src: International Shark Attack File, Florida Museum (2025 summary)

fresh.text: 2025 figures; the 2026 count comes out early in 2027

answers.q: Why are there so many sharks in Sydney?
also: Why are there so many sharks at the moment?
Why are there so many sharks in Australia?
Why are there so many sharks in Sydney Harbour?
answers.a: The sea off Sydney now stays warm enough for bull sharks for longer each year, and heavy rain draws them toward the coast.

answers.q: Why are there so many sharks in WA?
also: Why are there so many sharks in Perth at the moment?
Are shark attacks common in Perth?
How many shark attacks in WA this year?
answers.a: Recorded bites in WA have risen every decade, and almost half are white sharks. Why is only partly known.
detail: Unprovoked bites in WA: 7 in the 1990s, 23 in the 2000s, 41 in the 2010s and 44 from 2020 to 2025. WA's share of Australia's bites rose from 19% in the 2000s to 33% since 2020.
Of 108 WA bites since 2000, 50 were by white sharks, 17 by wobbegongs and 8 by bull sharks; 19 were fatal.
What's missing: how many more people are in the water, and WA's tagged-shark detections, which we've asked the state for.

answers.a: In warm coastal water and up rivers. In Australia, every one of 170 bull shark bites since 1900 happened where the sea was 19°C or warmer.
detail: They swim far up rivers: public sightings reach about 35 km up the Brisbane River and at least 120 km inland in Northern Territory rivers (straight-line distances). Elsewhere they've been found about 4,000 km up the Amazon, at Iquitos in Peru, and they live in Lake Nicaragua.

answers.q: When is shark season in Sydney?
also: When is shark season?
When is shark season in Australia?
answers.a: For bull sharks, the water off Sydney is warm enough from about late September to early July. That's about seven weeks longer than in the 1980s.
detail: Daily sea temperatures, 0.25° cell off Sydney: 19°C or warmer from about 25 September to 3 July in a typical recent year (2016–2025), against 30 October to 15 June in 1982–1992.
White and tiger sharks keep different seasons. This answer is for bull sharks.

answers.q: When is shark season in WA?
also: When is shark season in Perth?
When is shark season in Western Australia?
answers.a: There isn't a clear one. WA's bites come all year; around Perth, white shark bites cluster in spring.
detail: Perth area since 2000: 35 unprovoked bites, 15 of them by white sharks, and 7 of those 15 in October or November.
Across WA, white shark bites peak in March and October (7 each since 2000), but the numbers are small.
The 19°C bull shark season doesn't fit WA well: its main species is the white shark.

also: Why are shark attacks on the rise?
Are shark attacks increasing in Australia?
answers.a: Not worldwide in recent years: 2025's 65 confirmed bites were in line with the 2020–2024 average of 61. Some places are rising, though. In southern NSW, bites have grown faster than the coastal population.

answers.q: Is it safe to swim after heavy rain?
also: What attracts sharks?
answers.a: Better to wait. Official advice is to stay out of murky water after heavy rain, and most of the data points the same way.

also: Are bull sharks dangerous?
answers.a: Yes. Worldwide, about 8 people a year die from unprovoked shark bites. On Australia's coast, about 50 people drown for every shark death.
answers.src: International Shark Attack File; Surf Life Saving Australia; Australian Shark-Incident Database
see: Story: one shark death for every 50 drownings

also: Do shark nets stop shark attacks?
Do shark nets trap other animals?
answers.a: Not clear yet. The evidence is thin either way, but most of what the gear catches isn't one of the three sharks it targets.

also: Why are sharks endangered?
How many sharks are left?
Are bull sharks endangered?
answers.a: Many are. Bull sharks and great white sharks are listed as Vulnerable, and tiger sharks as Near Threatened.
detail: IUCN Red List: bull shark Vulnerable (assessed 2021, population decreasing), great white shark Vulnerable, tiger shark Near Threatened.
In the Mediterranean, white sharks are listed as Critically Endangered (IUCN regional assessment, 2016).
Oceanic sharks and rays have declined by 71% since 1970, mainly because fishing pressure rose about 18-fold (Pacoureau and colleagues, Nature, 2021).
About a third of shark and ray species are threatened with extinction.
answers.src: IUCN Red List; IUCN Mediterranean Red List (2016); Pacoureau et al. 2021

answers.q: What time of day do sharks attack?
also: When are sharks most active?
Are shark attacks more common at night?
answers.a: We can say when bites happen, not when the water is riskiest. That needs a count of people in the water by hour, which no one publishes.

answers.q: Was there a shark attack today?
also: Shark attack today
answers.a: This site doesn't report incidents as they happen. For today's sightings, bites and beach closures, check the official source where you are, or ask the lifeguards on the beach.

Cape Town: Shark Spotters.

Rare. In 2025 the US had 25 confirmed unprovoked bites, 1 of them fatal. Florida had 11, below its five-year average of 19, and Hawaii had 4. Hawaii's own list averages about 7 incidents a year since 2016, counting provoked ones too

part

Mississippi: rarely. A 2021 study confirmed two near St. Louis, in 1937 at Alton, Illinois, and in 1995 at Rush Island, Missouri; other reports were incomplete. Great Lakes and Lake Michigan: no records found, but the public data also misses the two Mississippi ones, so that isn't proof

Great white sharks in the Mediterranean, off Marseille
requin blanc Méditerranée · Marseille
part

Yes, but they're rarely seen, and they're listed as Critically Endangered there. Public records hold 58 white shark records across the Mediterranean, 24 of them since 2010, about half from the Aegean and Adriatic seas. The nearest to Marseille was a sighting about 16 km away in 2023; others were off the Var coast in 2012, 2015 and 2024. Most are public sightings that scientists haven't checked
